solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rent holiday place on the Adriatic

definitions.meaning: a rent is a tear or ... in cloth
A Croatian resort city on the Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: Someone is paying for a seaside apartment on the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment for the holiday place, but it is the noun meaning a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a rip or tear, the same as a split; Split is also a well-known Croatian coastal resort.

clue.text: Ancient trade route composed of dark soil

indicators.note: the route is said to be made up from these letters, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An old caravan road whose surface was made of black earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Silk Road was the network of overland trading paths linking China with the Mediterranean in antiquity.

clue.text: Hear about tragic king meeting knight

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A messenger hears news of an ill-fated monarch encountering a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to be told or hear about it; the two are synonyms for receiving news.

clue.text: Rival groups, leaderless, demand to enter thus

indicators.note: the shortened word is told to go into the other word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader is the front of a word, so the first letter of demand is dropped

explanation.surface: Warring factions without a head make demands to be let in, so it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' removes the opening letter, and 'to enter' sends what is left inside the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a divide between two opposed camps, an idiom for rival sides.

clue.text: Hang around some cathedral in Germany

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tourist idles near a German cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on or loiter, which is a synonym of hanging around.

clue.text: Trouble the setter is going to!

parts.note: a setter refers to themselves as I
'll is the contraction of will, meaning is going to

explanation.surface: The compiler cheerfully announces a plan to cause mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces read I'LL, the setter saying 'I will'; the apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill as a noun means harm or misfortune, so it can stand in for trouble.

clue.text: Old African colonel initially grinning as dull dignitaries all file in

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A smirking strongman watches a procession of tedious officials enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi, who ruled Libya until 2011, styled himself Colonel; Libya is in North Africa.

clue.text: Rock in river covering snakelike fish

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second, covering it

parts.note: an eel is a long fish shaped like a snake

explanation.surface: A stone in a stream sits above an eel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a noun for the stone, but it is the verb: to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or sway unsteadily, just as one might rock on one's feet.

clue.text: Post Office New York state's used for letter delivery system once

parts.note: to state is to express; the 's stands for 'is', joining to 'used for'

explanation.surface: A post office in New York state handles the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pony Express was a short-lived 1860s American mail service using relays of horse riders.

clue.text: European trapped in loo: self-esteem to drop!

indicators.note: the first piece is held inside the second, as if shut in

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a British word for loo
ego is a person's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A Continental stuck in a toilet is told to swallow their pride.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave go of something is to release your grip on it, so it means let it fall.

clue.text: See director general close to some gatekeeper's house

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A senior official is spotted near a small cottage by the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a small house at the entrance to an estate, traditionally lived in by the gatekeeper.

clue.text: Organise race series

definitions.meaning: to ... an event is to manage it
a ... is an unbroken sequence, as in a ... of wins

explanation.surface: An instruction to set up a sequence of races.
explanation.definitionFit: One short word covers managing something, a jog-race and a winning streak.

clue.text: Unusual to have year in exotic capital

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the rearranged word
exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters are taken into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller plans to spend a year in a foreign capital city, which is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the city word to ATPICAL; 'in' places the Y within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not representative of the norm, which is a synonym of out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Some wine Brian takes getting him drunk?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Brian drinks a little wine; is it making him tipsy?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: an inebriant is the thing doing the getting drunk, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriant is an intoxicating substance, something that makes a drinker tipsy.

clue.text: Harmony of form, a sort of m-mystery!

indicators.note: 'a sort of' says the letters are sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: A stammered word suggests a balanced shape is somehow puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'm-mystery' supplies the second M the anagram needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is the balanced correspondence of parts on either side of an axis, an aesthetic harmony.

clue.text: Daytime Brexit broadcast making use of both Left and Right?

definitions.text: making use of both Left and Right

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A daytime television programme on Brexit tries to give both political sides airtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left and Right' looks political, but it means the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambidexterity is the ability to use either hand equally well, hence employing both sides.

clue.text: British school's for French people

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, here with its 's

explanation.surface: An English school is set aside for students from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Bretons are the inhabitants of Brittany, a region of north-west France.

clue.text: One using ruler from Middle East, a certain king

parts.note: sure means certain
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch from the Middle East is wielding a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' looks like a king, but it is a measuring stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A person working with a ruler is taking measurements, so they are a measurer.

clue.text: Pickle — or something sweeter

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit preserve, sweeter than a pickled relish

explanation.surface: Choosing between a sour relish and a sweeter preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like the relish, but it is the sense 'tight spot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam means being in trouble, and jam is also a sugary spread.

clue.text: Comedian's "yes" to German upset salesperson

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesperson

explanation.surface: A comic agrees with a German who then upsets a sales rep.
explanation.definitionFit: A japer is someone who plays jokes or jests, a joker or comic.

clue.text: Ancient silver beads oddly missing

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are left out, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: An old silver necklace is missing some of its beads.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means very old, a straightforward synonym of ancient.

clue.text: No longer like to fall asleep, as alarm may?

definitions.meaning: an alarm goes off when it sounds

explanation.surface: Someone who once liked dozing finds the alarm clock's ring breaks their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers losing a liking, dozing off and a bell or siren sounding.

clue.text: Airmen coming north a long way

indicators.note: in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Pilots are flying north over a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means distant, a long way off.

clue.text: Stick flexible as putty

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so these letters are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A rod as pliable as putty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to stay in place without moving, the same as to stay put.

clue.text: Something sandy or maroon?

definitions.meaning: to maroon someone is to abandon or ... them

explanation.surface: Is a sandy place also reddish-brown?
explanation.walkthrough: 'maroon' looks like the colour, but it is the verb meaning strand.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is an arid sandy region; to desert someone is to abandon them as a castaway is marooned.

clue.text: Like pitch Jack's seen near railway

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so Jack gives tar; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A sailor is spotted beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black tar-like substance, so something resembling it is tarry.
